task_instance: Run the /search command's core deliverable: given a query like 'what did we decide on the API redesign', check for connected MCP sources (chat, email, cloud storage, project tracker, CRM, knowledge base), decompose the query, run parallel searches across those sources, deduplicate/rank, and synthesize a unified answer with source attribution.
blocker_detail: The skill's entire mechanism (steps 1, 3, 4) depends on querying connected MCP sources such as chat platforms, email, cloud storage, project trackers, CRM, or knowledge-base tools, and synthesizing/deduplicating results across them. The developer runtime described for this task grants only: file read/write, shell commands, local dev servers/tests, browser automation, and conversation -- it grants no ability to query any external chat/email/CRM/cloud-storage/project-tracker/knowledge-base source. The task instructions also explicitly forbid calling any connector or MCP tool (Notion, Google Drive, GitHub, Slack, Jam, Mem, Bigdata, etc.) even though several appear in the tool list, so even a live-connector approach is off-limits. There is no local, non-MCP substitute available in this runtime that would exercise the skill's real function (cross-source federated search over already-connected workplace tools) rather than a superficial keyword-grep over synthetic files, which would not actually test or demonstrate the skill's core intent (querying and reconciling *actually connected* live sources). Since the sandbox provides zero connected sources to search in the first place, step 1 of the skill ('Check Available Sources') would correctly conclude no sources are connected and the skill would emit its own 'no sources connected' message -- meaning the skill's core deliverable (a synthesized, multi-source answer) cannot be produced at all in this environment.
evidence: Read the skill document at /home/user/skill-achievability-compiler/benchmark/ce_sources_div/anthropics__knowledge-work-plugins__search/SKILL.md. It defines /search as a command that enumerates connected MCP sources (chat, email, cloud storage, project tracker, CRM, knowledge base), builds per-source sub-queries, executes them in parallel via those tools, and synthesizes a deduplicated, ranked, attributed answer -- with an explicit fallback message when 'no MCP sources are connected'. The developer-sandbox runtime description for this task lists only file/shell/browser/local-dev abilities, no connector access, and the task's safety rules explicitly prohibit invoking any MCP/connector tool (Notion, Google Drive, GitHub, Slack, Jam, Mem, Bigdata, or any mcp__* tool) even where present in the tool list. Because the skill's only real deliverable is a live search across such connected sources, and no such source can be connected or queried here, the task cannot be attempted beyond confirming (per the skill's own step 1 logic) that zero sources are available. No files beyond this result.json were created since faking mock 'chat/email' text files and grepping them would not exercise the skill's actual claimed capability (querying real connected workplace tools) and was avoided per the instruction not to work around a genuine blocker.
